extra_misconceptions.fact: Xylem transports water and minerals upward from the roots, whereas phloem moves sugars from the leaves to growing tissues.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Xylem and phloem carry water and dissolved sugars in both directions interchangeably throughout the plant stem.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Root hairs are single-cell extensions of the root epidermis that live only a few days to absorb water and dissolved minerals.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Root hairs are miniature lateral roots that eventually thicken into woody anchor roots as the plant matures.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Petals attract pollinators visually and by scent, while the anthers produce pollen and the ovary houses the ovules inside.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Brightly colored flower petals directly produce the pollen grains and ovules required for seed fertilization.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Roots only absorb mineral ions dissolved in soil water, while carbon from air builds the vast majority of plant tissue.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plant roots absorb solid soil particles directly into the vascular system to build new stems and foliage.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to water transport in a stem if the xylem vessels are severed during a cross-section cut?
Which structural feature distinguishes a flower's pollen-producing stamen from its seed-bearing pistil?
What scale notation on your botanical sketch confirms the actual millimeter length of the specimen's sepals?
Why is it dangerous to dissect unknown wild plant stems or bulbs with bare hands before verifying their species?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Plant cells respire continuously day and night to power metabolism, while photosynthesis occurs only when light is available.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plants perform photosynthesis during daylight hours and only switch to cellular respiration after the sun sets.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Photosynthesis releases oxygen by splitting water molecules during the light-dependent reactions inside the chloroplasts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The oxygen gas released during photosynthesis comes directly from splitting absorbed carbon dioxide molecules.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue wavelengths of light while reflecting green light back to the viewer's eyes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Green leaves absorb green wavelengths of sunlight most efficiently to drive sugar synthesis in chlorophyll.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Nearly all dry biomass in a tree is built from carbon and oxygen atoms fixed from atmospheric carbon dioxide gas.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Most of the dry weight of a mature oak tree comes from mineral nutrients pulled up out of the forest soil.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to oxygen output if you submerge an aquatic leaf in plain tap water lacking dissolved carbon dioxide?
Under what condition does a green plant's cellular respiration rate exceed its photosynthetic sugar production?
What measurement confirms that stomatal guard cells have closed on the underside of a sun-stressed leaf?
Where should a Scout position a hot grow lamp during a photosynthesis trial to prevent leaf scorch and electrical shorts?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bees forage strictly to collect sugary nectar and protein-rich pollen for their hive, transferring pollen grains by accident.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Honeybees visit flowers intentionally to fertilize the plant's ovules so that new seeds and fruits can develop.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cereal grains such as corn, wheat, oats, and rice rely on wind pollination rather than insects to fertilize their flowers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All agricultural crops require honeybee or native insect pollination in order to produce harvestable grain or fruit.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Forager bees moisten dry pollen with regurgitated nectar to form sticky pellets that cling to their hind-leg pollen baskets.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Worker honeybees pack dry pollen grains onto their hind legs using only static electricity from their flight muscles.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Systemic and residual insecticides can contaminate morning dew, nectar, and pollen for days after an evening application.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Spraying broad-spectrum insecticides at dusk eliminates all risk to honeybees foraging in an orchard the next morning.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to fruit set in a squash patch if rain or netting blocks insect visits during the morning bloom window?
Which physical indicator distinguishes sticky insect-carried pollen grains from lightweight wind-dispersed pollen?
What timed count per square meter lets you log pollinator visitation rates accurately across two flowering plots?
Why is it dangerous to wear dark fuzzy clothing or scented lotion while observing an active honeybee foraging patch?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Organic matter improves soil structure and pore space, but soil texture depends strictly on fixed sand, silt, and clay ratios.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding generous amounts of compost or peat moss permanently changes a heavy clay soil's mineral texture into loam.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Waterlogged soil fills pore spaces and suffocates roots by cutting off the oxygen needed for nutrient uptake and respiration.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Overwatered plants wilt and die because their root cells absorb too much water and burst from internal pressure.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Working wet clay crushes natural pore channels and creates dense, brick-like clods that block root growth and water percolation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Double-digging or rototilling wet clay soil in early spring loosens the ground and improves root drainage all season.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excess nitrogen stimulates soft, leafy shoot growth at the expense of flowers and fruit while making tissue prone to aphid attack.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying extra synthetic nitrogen fertilizer to a nutrient-deficient bed always accelerates flowering and fruit ripening.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the sand, silt, and clay layers in a jar test if you take your depth readings after only ten minutes?
Which soil property distinguishes permanent mineral texture from the crumb structure built by organic matter and roots?
What pH reading on your soil test log indicates that iron and phosphorus are locked up in insoluble mineral forms?
Why is it dangerous to mix dry lime, bone meal, or dusty compost in a closed shed without eye protection and a dust mask?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Seeds result from sexual genetic recombination, whereas only asexual cuttings or grafts produce exact clones of a hybrid parent.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Planting seeds saved from a hybrid apple or tomato guarantees offspring with identical fruit traits to the parent plant.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Successful grafting requires tight contact between the thin vascular cambium layers of the scion and rootstock to bridge new vessels.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Grafting joins the outer bark and central woody pith of two stems so that sap can mix freely through the heartwood.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dipping cuttings directly into the stock container contaminates the remaining hormone powder with plant sap and disease pathogens.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dipping a stem cutting deep into the main bottle of rooting hormone powder prevents fungal rot across your whole flat.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Each potato seed piece must contain at least one dormant bud eye on the skin surface to generate new shoots and roots.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any cut piece of a potato tuber will sprout a new plant as long as it contains enough white starchy flesh for energy.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a whip-and-tongue graft if the scion's green cambium ring does not align with the rootstock's cambium?
Which anatomical feature distinguishes a true stem tuber like a potato from a swollen storage root like a sweet potato?
What daily soil temperature and moisture entries in your propagation log explain why a tray of seeds failed to sprout?
Why is it dangerous to take stem cuttings across multiple plants without wiping your grafting knife with rubbing alcohol?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most non-native crop and garden plants remain confined to cultivated beds, whereas invasive species spread aggressively into wild ecosystems.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every non-native plant introduced from another continent is an invasive species that harms local wildlife habitat.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Home compost piles rarely reach temperatures hot enough to kill hardy weed seeds or root fragments, spreading them when compost is used.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tossing pulled invasive weeds containing ripe seeds or rhizomes onto a backyard compost pile destroys their viability.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Disturbed soil and increased sunlight trigger dormant invasive seeds in the soil seed bank, requiring multi-year monitoring and weeding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Clearing an invasive shrub stand in a single afternoon permanently restores the native forest understory without follow-up.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Biological control agents undergo years of quarantine host-specificity testing to verify they will not attack native plants or crops.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Releasing any plant-eating beetle or fungus from an invasive weed's home range is a fast, risk-free biological control.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to an invasive weed patch if you pull mature plants after their seed heads have already dried and opened?
Under what ecological condition does a non-native garden ornamental cross the threshold into an invasive species?
What GPS coordinates and canopy-cover percentages in your field notebook track whether a weed removal plot is recovering?
Where should a Scout inspect boots, socks, and trouser cuffs before leaving an invasive grass trail to stop seed spread?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Plant scientists work in molecular genetics, pathology, precision satellite agronomy, forestry, habitat restoration, and turf management.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Professional plant science careers are limited to traditional family farming or working at a retail garden center.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many skilled roles such as certified arborists, irrigation specialists, and nursery managers enter through two-year degrees and exams.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every career in horticulture, arboriculture, or crop management requires a four-year university bachelor's degree.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Field agronomists and pathologists split their time between outdoor crop scouting, soil sampling, and laboratory diagnostics.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Agronomists and plant pathologists spend their entire workweek indoors running laboratory tests on pressed leaves.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Professional agricultural and arborist certifications require ongoing continuing education credits to stay current on safety and science.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: State pesticide applicator licenses and Certified Crop Adviser credentials remain valid for life without renewal hours.

extra_socratic_questions: What step must you complete with your parent or guardian before contacting an agronomist or botanist for an interview?
Which daily field responsibility distinguishes a commercial crop agronomist from a botanical garden taxonomist?
What license, certification, and seasonal wage figures should you record when comparing two plant science career tracks?
Why is it dangerous to tour a research greenhouse or seed-treatment facility without asking about restricted-entry signs?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Divide sprouted seeds by 50 and multiply by 100, so 40 sprouted seeds out of 50 equals an 80 percent germination rate.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A germination test count of 40 sprouted seeds out of 50 tested seeds equals a 40 percent germination rate for that lot.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Submerging crop seeds in standing water starves the embryos of oxygen and promotes bacterial rot instead of normal sprouting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Soaking test seeds underwater in a jar for a full week speeds up germination and improves your final sprout percentage.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Over-tilled powdery soil crusts hard after rain, blocking seedling emergence and accelerating wind and water erosion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulverizing a field seedbed into fine, powdery dust ensures the best moisture absorption and fastest seedling emergence.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only seedlings with both a healthy primary root and an intact shoot meristem count as normal viable sprouts in agronomy tests.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any seed that cracks its seed coat during a germination trial counts as a viable seedling ready for field production.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your 50-seed rag-doll germination test if you seal the rolled paper towel inside an airtight plastic bag?
Which visual trait distinguishes a vigorous normal seedling from an abnormal sprout that will fail in a field seedbed?
What calculation converts the sprouted count from your 50-seed trial into an adjusted field seeding rate per acre?
Why is it dangerous to handle pink or blue fungicide-coated crop seeds for a germination test without nitrile gloves?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Harvesting plants in protected parks is illegal and depletes seed sources needed by pollinators and future plant generations.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Collecting a single wildflower from a national park trail is harmless because thousands of identical blooms grow nearby.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Footprints crush fragile root systems and biological soil crusts that can take decades to regenerate in harsh environments.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Walking off-trail across alpine tundra or cryptobiotic soil crusts causes only temporary flattening that recovers after rain.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Detailed field sketches and scaled photographs of leaves, stems, and flowers document plant identity while leaving flora intact.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pressing a physical plant specimen is always required to verify a wild species identification for a merit badge field notebook.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rotting food scraps alter local soil chemistry, introduce non-native seeds, and attract wildlife that trample native vegetation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Discarding apple cores or orange peels in the woods benefits native plants because fruit waste is natural and biodegradable.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to native plant communities if you hike between study plots without brushing invasive seeds from your boot treads?
Under what condition does a botanical survey permit physical voucher clipping instead of non-destructive macro photography?
What field log data allows you to identify a rare orchid later without pressing a live specimen or trampling surrounding moss?
Why is it dangerous to native flora when a Scout uses unsterilized pruning shears across multiple wild plant populations?
